title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Solution Formation
text:
Solution Formation

Key terms: solvent, solute, homogeneous

A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components, where the component present in the largest quantity is the solvent, determining the physical state of the solution. The other components are solutes.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Solution Formation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Concentration Units
text:
Concentration Units

Key terms: mass percentage, volume percentage, mole fraction, molarity

Concentration of a solution can be expressed in various units such as mass percentage (w/w), volume percentage (V/V), mass by volume percentage (w/V), parts per million (ppm), mole fraction, and molarity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Concentration Units in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Henry's Law
text:
Henry's Law

Key terms: Henry's law, partial pressure, solubility

Henry's law states that at a constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of the liquid or solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Henry's Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Solubility
text:
Solubility

Key terms: solubility, solute, solvent

Solubility is the maximum amount of a substance that can be dissolved in a specified amount of solvent at a specified temperature. It depends on the nature of the solute and solvent, as well as temperature and pressure.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Solubility in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Effect of Temperature on Solubility
text:
Effect of Temperature on Solubility

Key terms: temperature, solubility, endothermic, exothermic

The solubility of a solid in a liquid is significantly affected by temperature changes. In general, if the dissolution process is endothermic, the solubility increases with a rise in temperature, and if it is exothermic, the solubility decreases.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Effect of Temperature on Solubility in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Effect of Pressure on Solubility of Gases
text:
Effect of Pressure on Solubility of Gases

Key terms: pressure, solubility, Henry's law

The solubility of gases in liquids is greatly affected by pressure. The solubility of a gas increases with an increase in pressure, as shown by Henry's law.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Effect of Pressure on Solubility of Gases
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Effect of Pressure on Solubility of Gases in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Henry's Law
text:
Henry's Law

Key terms: Henry's Law, solubility, partial pressure

At constant temp, gas solubility in liquid is directly proportional to its partial pressure. Math: p = KH * x.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Henry's Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Henry's Law Constant (KH)
text:
Henry's Law Constant (KH)

Key terms: Henry's Law Constant, KH, temperature

Proportionality constant in Henry's Law. Different gases have different KH values at same temp.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Henry's Law Constant (KH) in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Solubility of Gases in Liquids
text:
Solubility of Gases in Liquids

Key terms: solubility, pressure, temperature

Increases with increase in pressure and decreases with increase in temperature.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Solubility of Gases in Liquids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Raoult's Law
text:
Raoult's Law

Key terms: Raoult's Law, vapour pressure, mole fraction

Partial vapour pressure of each component in solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Raoult's Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ideal Solutions
text:
Ideal Solutions

Key terms: ideal solutions, Raoult's law, enthalpy of mixing

Obey Raoult's law, enthalpy of mixing is zero, and volume of mixing is zero.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ideal Solutions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ideal Solutions
text:
Ideal Solutions

Key terms: Raoult's law, intermolecular forces

Solutions where intermolecular forces between A-A, B-B, and A-B are nearly equal, leading to ideal behavior and obeying Raoult's law.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ideal Solutions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Non-Ideal Solutions
text:
Non-Ideal Solutions

Key terms: Raoult's law, positive deviation, negative deviation

Solutions that do not obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration, exhibiting positive or negative deviations.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Non-Ideal Solutions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Colligative Properties
text:
Colligative Properties

Key terms: vapour pressure, boiling point, freezing point, osmotic pressure

Properties of solutions that depend only on the number of solute particles, such as relative lowering of vapour pressure, boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, and osmotic pressure.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Colligative Properties in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure
text:
Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure

Key terms: vapour pressure, mole fraction, solute

The decrease in vapour pressure of a solvent when a non-volatile solute is added, which depends on the mole fraction of the solute.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Elevation of Boiling Point
text:
Elevation of Boiling Point

Key terms: boiling point, molality, solute

The increase in boiling point of a solvent when a non-volatile solute is added, which is directly proportional to the molality of the solute.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Elevation of Boiling Point in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Depression of Freezing Point
text:
Depression of Freezing Point

Key terms: freezing point, molality, solute

The decrease in freezing point of a solvent when a non-volatile solute is added, which is directly proportional to the molality of the solute.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Depression of Freezing Point in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Azeotropes
text:
Azeotropes

Key terms: azeotrope, binary mixture, fractional distillation

Binary mixtures that have the same composition in the liquid and vapour phases, boiling at a constant temperature, and cannot be separated by fractional distillation.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Azeotropes in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molality and Molarity
text:
Molality and Molarity

Key terms: molality, molarity, solvent, solute

Molality is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent, while molarity is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. Both are important in understanding the behavior of solutions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Molality and Molarity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Colligative Properties
text:
Colligative Properties

Key terms: colligative properties, boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, osmotic pressure

Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles present in a solution, not their identity. Examples include boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, and osmotic pressure.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Colligative Properties in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molal Boiling Point Elevation and Freezing Point Depression Constants
text:
Molal Boiling Point Elevation and Freezing Point Depression Constants

Key terms: Kb, Kf, solvent, solute

These constants (Kb and Kf) measure the change in boiling or freezing point of a solution per mole of solute. They depend on the nature of the solvent.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Molal Boiling Point Elevation and Freezing Point Depression Constants
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Molal Boiling Point Elevation and Freezing Point Depression Constants in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Determining Molar Mass Using Colligative Properties
text:
Determining Molar Mass Using Colligative Properties

Key terms: molar mass, colligative properties, Kb, Kf

The molar mass of a solute can be calculated using colligative properties like boiling point elevation or freezing point depression, along with the molal boiling point elevation or freezing point depression constant.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Determining Molar Mass Using Colligative Properties
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Determining Molar Mass Using Colligative Properties in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Osmosis and Osmotic Pressure
text:
Osmosis and Osmotic Pressure

Key terms: osmosis, osmotic pressure, semipermeable membrane

Osmosis is the movement of solvent molecules from a region of low solute concentration to a region of high solute concentration through a semipermeable membrane. Osmotic pressure is the pressure required to stop this movement.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Osmosis and Osmotic Pressure in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
text:
Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass

Key terms: van't Hoff factor, abnormal molar mass, association, dissociation

The van't Hoff factor (i) accounts for the extent of dissociation or association of solute molecules. Abnormal molar mass is the experimentally determined molar mass that is either lower or higher than the expected value due to association or dissociation.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Van't Hoff Factor (i)
text:
Van't Hoff Factor (i)

Key terms: van't Hoff factor, colligative property

The van't Hoff factor (i) is a measure of the number of particles into which a solute dissociates in solution. It's calculated as the ratio of the observed colligative property to the calculated colligative property.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Van't Hoff Factor (i) in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Dissociation of Benzoic Acid
text:
Dissociation of Benzoic Acid

Key terms: benzoic acid, dissociation, van't Hoff factor

Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) dissociates in solution to form benzoate ions (C6H5COO-) and hydrogen ions (H+). The degree of dissociation can be calculated using the van't Hoff factor.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Dissociation of Benzoic Acid in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Henry's Law
text:
Henry's Law

Key terms: Henry's law, gas solubility, partial pressure

Henry's law states that at a given temperature, the amount of a gas that dissolves in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas above the liquid.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Henry's Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Raoult's Law
text:
Raoult's Law

Key terms: Raoult's law, vapour pressure, mole fraction

Raoult's law states that the relative lowering of the vapour pressure of a solvent in a solution is equal to the mole fraction of the solute present in the solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Raoult's Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Colligative Properties
text:
Colligative Properties

Key terms: colligative properties, boiling point elevation, freezing point depression

Colligative properties are properties of solutions that depend only on the number of solute particles and not on their chemical identity. Examples include boiling point elevation, freezing point depression, and osmotic pressure.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Colligative Properties in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molarity
text:
Molarity

Key terms: molarity, concentration, solution

Molarity is a measure of the concentration of a solution, defined as the number of moles of solute per liter of solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Molarity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molality
text:
Molality

Key terms: molality, concentration, solution

Molality is a measure of the concentration of a solution, defined as the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Molality in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Mole Fraction
text:
Mole Fraction

Key terms: mole fraction, composition, mixture

Mole fraction is a measure of the composition of a mixture, defined as the number of moles of a component divided by the total number of moles of all components in the mixture.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Mole Fraction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Galvanic vs Electrolytic Cells
text:
Galvanic vs Electrolytic Cells

Key terms: galvanic cell, electrolytic cell, cell potential, external voltage

Galvanic cells convert chemical energy to electrical energy, while electrolytic cells use electrical energy to drive non-spontaneous chemical reactions. In a galvanic cell, the reaction stops when the external voltage equals the cell potential, and reverses when the external voltage exceeds it.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Galvanic vs Electrolytic Cells in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Nernst Equation
text:
Nernst Equation

Key terms: Nernst equation, electrode potential, standard electrode potential (E°), electromotive force (emf)

The Nernst equation relates the electrode potential of a galvanic cell to the concentrations of the reactants and products in the cell. It allows for the calculation of the cell's electromotive force (emf) at any concentration, given the standard electrode potential (E°).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Nernst Equation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Standard Potential of a Cell
text:
Standard Potential of a Cell

Key terms: standard potential of a cell, reduction potential, oxidation potential, standard state

The standard potential of a cell is the potential difference between the reduction potential of the cathode and the oxidation potential of the anode, when all reactants and products are at standard state (1 M concentration, 1 bar pressure, and 25°C temperature).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Standard Potential of a Cell in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Resistivity and Conductivity
text:
Resistivity and Conductivity

Key terms: resistivity (ρ), conductivity (k), molar conductivity (Λm)

Resistivity (ρ) is the resistance of a material per unit length and unit cross-sectional area, while conductivity (k) is the reciprocal of resistivity. Molar conductivity (Λm) is the conductivity of a solution per mole of solute.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Resistivity and Conductivity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionic vs Electronic Conductivity
text:
Ionic vs Electronic Conductivity

Key terms: ionic conductivity, electronic conductivity, semiconductors

Ionic conductivity occurs in electrolytic solutions due to the movement of ions, while electronic conductivity occurs in metals due to the movement of electrons. Some materials, like semiconductors, exhibit both types of conductivity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ionic vs Electronic Conductivity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Measurement of Conductivity
text:
Measurement of Conductivity

Key terms: conductivity meter, alternating current, electrode polarization, molar conductivity (Λm)

The conductivity of an electrolytic solution can be measured using a conductivity meter, which applies an alternating current to prevent electrode polarization. Molar conductivity can be calculated from conductivity using the formula: Λm = k / C, where k is the conductivity and C is the concentration of the electrolyte.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Measurement of Conductivity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Kohlrausch Law
text:
Kohlrausch Law

Key terms: Kohlrausch law, molar conductivity at infinite dilution (Λ°), ions

Kohlrausch's law states that the molar conductivity of an electrolyte at infinite dilution (Λ°) is the sum of the molar conductivities of its ions at infinite dilution (Λ°). This law allows for the calculation of the molar conductivity of an electrolyte from the molar conductivities of its ions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Kohlrausch Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Nernst Equation
text:
Nernst Equation

Key terms: electrode potential, concentration, redox reaction

Relates the electrode potential of a redox reaction to the concentrations of reactants and products. Used to calculate cell potential under non-standard conditions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Nernst Equation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Standard Electrode Potential
text:
Standard Electrode Potential

Key terms: redox reaction, spontaneity, standard conditions

Measures the tendency of a redox reaction to occur spontaneously under standard conditions (1 M concentration, 298 K). Used to determine the spontaneity of a reaction.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Standard Electrode Potential in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electrochemical Cell and Gibbs Energy
text:
Electrochemical Cell and Gibbs Energy

Key terms: emf, Gibbs energy, equilibrium constant

Relates the emf of an electrochemical cell to the Gibbs energy change of the reaction it represents. Used to calculate the equilibrium constant of a reaction.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electrochemical Cell and Gibbs Energy in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions
text:
Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions

Key terms: ionic solution, conductivity, electrolyte

Measures the ability of an ionic solution to conduct electricity. Depends on the nature of the electrolyte, concentration, temperature, and other factors.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Measurement of Ionic Solution Conductivity
text:
Measurement of Ionic Solution Conductivity

Key terms: alternating current, conductivity cell, resistance

Uses an alternating current source and a conductivity cell to accurately measure the resistance of an ionic solution without changing its composition.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Measurement of Ionic Solution Conductivity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Alternating Current (AC) for Conductivity Measurements
text:
Alternating Current (AC) for Conductivity Measurements

Key terms: alternating current, conductivity cell, resistance, conductivity

AC is used instead of DC to avoid changing the solution's composition. A conductivity cell with platinum electrodes is used to measure resistance, which is then converted to conductivity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Alternating Current (AC) for Conductivity Measurements in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Cell Constant (G*) Determination
text:
Cell Constant (G*) Determination

Key terms: cell constant, conductivity, resistance

The cell constant, G*, is determined using a solution with known conductivity, like KCl. It's calculated as the ratio of the solution's conductivity to its resistance in the cell.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Cell Constant (G*) Determination in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Conductivity (k) and Molar Conductivity (Lm)
text:
Conductivity (k) and Molar Conductivity (Lm)

Key terms: conductivity, molar conductivity, electrolyte

Conductivity, k, is the ability of a solution to conduct electricity, measured in S m–1 or S cm–1. Molar conductivity, Lm, is the conductivity of a solution containing one mole of electrolyte, measured in S m2 mol–1 or S cm2 mol–1.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Conductivity (k) and Molar Conductivity (Lm) in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Conductivity Measurement Setup
text:
Conductivity Measurement Setup

Key terms: Wheatstone bridge, resistance, conductivity cell

A Wheatstone bridge is used to measure the resistance of a solution in a conductivity cell. The bridge is balanced when no current passes through the detector, and the unknown resistance is calculated using the bridge's equation.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Conductivity Measurement Setup in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions
text:
Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions

Key terms: Kohlrausch's law, limiting molar conductivity, electrolyte

Kohlrausch's law states that the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the individual contributions of the anion and cation. This law is used to calculate L°m for electrolytes and weak electrolytes.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electrolysis of Copper Sulphate
text:
Electrolysis of Copper Sulphate

Key terms: electrolysis, cathode, anode, copper sulphate

When a DC voltage is applied to a solution of copper sulphate with two copper electrodes, copper metal is deposited on the cathode (negative electrode) and copper is dissolved at the anode (positive electrode). This process is used to purify copper.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Electrolysis of Copper Sulphate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis
text:
Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis

Key terms: Faraday's laws, electrolysis, chemical equivalent weight

Faraday's laws state that the amount of chemical reaction occurring at an electrode during electrolysis is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed, and the amounts of different substances liberated are proportional to their chemical equivalent weights.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electrochemical Reduction of Metals
text:
Electrochemical Reduction of Metals

Key terms: electrochemical reduction, electrolysis, metals

Many metals like Na, Mg, Al, etc. are produced on a large scale by the electrochemical reduction of their respective cations using electrolysis, where no suitable chemical reducing agents are available.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Electrochemical Reduction of Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Quantitative Aspects of Electrolysis
text:
Quantitative Aspects of Electrolysis

Key terms: quantitative aspects, electrolysis, Faraday's laws

The charge passed through the electrolytic cell during electrolysis is equal to the product of current in amperes and time in seconds. The mass of a substance deposited or dissolved can be calculated using Faraday's laws.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Quantitative Aspects of Electrolysis in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Products of Electrolysis
text:
Products of Electrolysis

Key terms: products of electrolysis, electrodes, chemical reaction

The products of electrolysis depend on the nature of the material being electrolysed and the type of electrodes used. Inert electrodes do not participate in the chemical reaction, while reactive electrodes do.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Products of Electrolysis in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Batteries
text:
Batteries

Key terms: batteries, galvanic cells, primary batteries, secondary batteries

Batteries are galvanic cells that convert chemical energy into electrical energy. Primary batteries are used once and then discarded, while secondary batteries can be recharged.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Batteries in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Fuel Cells
text:
Fuel Cells

Key terms: fuel cells, combustion, electrical energy

Fuel cells directly convert the energy of combustion of fuels like hydrogen, methane, methanol, etc. into electrical energy. They are highly efficient and pollution-free.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Fuel Cells in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Corrosion
text:
Corrosion

Key terms: corrosion, metallic surfaces, oxidation

Corrosion is the slow coating of metallic surfaces with oxides or other salts of the metal, causing damage to objects made of metals. It can be caused by atmospheric oxidation or other chemical reactions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Corrosion in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Fuel Cells
text:
Fuel Cells

Key terms: fuel cells, hydrogen, electricity, pollution-free

Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, are pollution-free, and are being developed for use in automobiles. They work by combining hydrogen and oxygen to produce water and electricity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Fuel Cells in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Corrosion
text:
Corrosion

Key terms: corrosion, metals, environment, prevention

Corrosion is the damage of metals due to chemical reactions with their environment, often involving oxygen and water. It causes significant economic losses and can be prevented by protecting metal surfaces.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Corrosion in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Rusting of Iron
text:
Rusting of Iron

Key terms: rusting, iron, oxygen, water, prevention

Rusting of iron is a type of corrosion where iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide (rust). It occurs in the presence of water and air and can be prevented by protecting iron surfaces.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Rusting of Iron in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Hydrogen Economy
text:
Hydrogen Economy

Key terms: Hydrogen Economy, hydrogen, renewable, non-polluting, fuel cells

The Hydrogen Economy is a vision where hydrogen is used as a renewable and non-polluting source of energy. It is produced by splitting water using solar energy and used in fuel cells to generate electricity.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Hydrogen Economy in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electrochemical Cell
text:
Electrochemical Cell

Key terms: electrochemical cell, anode, cathode, electrolytic solution

An electrochemical cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy or vice versa. It consists of two electrodes (anode and cathode) dipped in an electrolytic solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrochemical Cell in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Galvanic Cell
text:
Galvanic Cell

Key terms: galvanic cell, redox reaction, electrical work, metals, salt solutions

A galvanic cell is a type of electrochemical cell where a spontaneous redox reaction is used to produce electrical work. It consists of two different metals dipped in their salt solutions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Galvanic Cell in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electrolytic Cell
text:
Electrolytic Cell

Key terms: electrolytic cell, redox reaction, electrical energy, electrodes, electrolytic solution

An electrolytic cell is a type of electrochemical cell where electrical energy is used to carry out a non-spontaneous redox reaction. It consists of two identical electrodes dipped in an electrolytic solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electrolytic Cell in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Standard Electrode Potential
text:
Standard Electrode Potential

Key terms: standard electrode potential, redox reaction, standard conditions, standard cell potential

Standard electrode potential is the measure of the tendency of a redox reaction to occur under standard conditions. It is measured in volts (V) and is used to calculate the standard cell potential.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Standard Electrode Potential in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Average Rate of Reaction
text:
Average Rate of Reaction

Key terms: average rate, concentration, time

Average rate is the change in concentration of reactants or products divided by the time taken. It's calculated over a specific time interval.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Average Rate of Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Instantaneous Rate of Reaction
text:
Instantaneous Rate of Reaction

Key terms: instantaneous rate, limit, time interval

Instantaneous rate is the rate at a particular moment in time, calculated as the limit of average rate as time interval approaches zero.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Instantaneous Rate of Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Rate Law
text:
Rate Law

Key terms: rate law, rate of reaction, concentration

Rate law is an expression that relates the rate of a reaction to the concentration of reactants, with each term raised to some power.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Rate Law in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Rate Constant
text:
Rate Constant

Key terms: rate constant, rate law, reaction speed

Rate constant (k) is a proportionality constant in the rate law, representing the speed of a reaction under specific conditions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Rate Constant in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Dependence of Rate on Concentration
text:
Dependence of Rate on Concentration

Key terms: rate, concentration, reaction rate

The rate of a reaction depends on the concentration of reactants. Increasing concentration generally increases the reaction rate.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Dependence of Rate on Concentration in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Rate Law and Order of Reaction
text:
Rate Law and Order of Reaction

Key terms: Rate Law, Order of Reaction, Rate Constant

Rate law describes how reaction rate depends on reactant concentrations. Order of reaction is the sum of exponents in rate law, indicating reaction's sensitivity to concentration changes.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Rate Law and Order of Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rate Law and Order of Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Zero Order Reaction
text:
Zero Order Reaction

Key terms: Zero Order, Rate Constant, Initial Concentration

In zero order reactions, reaction rate is independent of reactant concentration. Rate = k, and [A] = [A]0 - kt.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Zero Order Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | First Order Reaction
text:
First Order Reaction

Key terms: First Order, Rate Constant, Concentration

In first order reactions, reaction rate is proportional to the concentration of one reactant. Rate = k[A], and ln[A] = -kt + ln[A]0.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to First Order Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molecularity of a Reaction
text:
Molecularity of a Reaction

Key terms: Molecularity, Elementary Reaction, Unimolecular, Bimolecular, Termolecular

Molecularity is the number of reacting species involved in an elementary reaction. It can be unimolecular (1), bimolecular (2), or termolecular (3) or higher.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Molecularity of a Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Half-Life of a Reaction
text:
Half-Life of a Reaction

Key terms: Half-Life, First Order Reaction, Rate Constant

Half-life is the time taken for the concentration of a reactant to decrease to half of its initial value. For first order reactions, t1/2 = 0.693/k.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Half-Life of a Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Integrated Rate Equations
text:
Integrated Rate Equations

Key terms: Integrated Rate Equation, Zero Order, First Order, Half-Life

Integrated rate equations relate concentration changes over time for different reaction orders, allowing calculation of rate constants and half-lives.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Integrated Rate Equations in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Half-Life of a First Order Reaction
text:
Half-Life of a First Order Reaction

Key terms: half-life, first order reaction, rate constant

The time taken for a reaction to reach half of its maximum yield is called half-life. For a first order reaction, half-life is independent of initial concentration and can be calculated using the formula t1/2 = 0.693/k.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Half-Life of a First Order Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Half-Life of a First Order Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Time for Completion of a First Order Reaction
text:
Time for Completion of a First Order Reaction

Key terms: first order reaction, half-life, completion time

In a first order reaction, the time required for completion of 99.9% is 10 times the half-life of the reaction. This can be calculated using the formula t = 6.909/k.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Time for Completion of a First Order Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Time for Completion of a First Order Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate
text:
Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate

Key terms: reaction rate, temperature, Arrhenius equation

The rate of a chemical reaction increases with temperature. The temperature dependence of the rate can be explained by the Arrhenius equation, k = A * e^(-Ea/RT).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Pseudo First Order Reactions
text:
Pseudo First Order Reactions

Key terms: pseudo first order reaction, hydrolysis, ethyl acetate

Some reactions, though higher order, behave like first order reactions under certain conditions. These are called pseudo first order reactions. An example is the hydrolysis of ethyl acetate.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Pseudo First Order Reactions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions
text:
Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions

Key terms: collision theory, reaction rate, effective collisions

Collision theory explains that a chemical reaction occurs when reactant molecules collide with sufficient energy and proper orientation. The rate of reaction is determined by the collision frequency and the probability of effective collisions.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Effect of Temperature on Rate Constant
text:
Effect of Temperature on Rate Constant

Key terms: Arrhenius equation, rate constant, temperature

Increasing temperature speeds up chemical reactions. The Arrhenius equation (k = Ae-Ea/RT) shows this relationship, where k is the rate constant, A is the Arrhenius factor, Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Effect of Temperature on Rate Constant
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Effect of Temperature on Rate Constant in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Calculating Activation Energy (Ea)
text:
Calculating Activation Energy (Ea)

Key terms: Arrhenius equation, activation energy, rate constant

Ea can be calculated using the Arrhenius equation. If the rate of a reaction doubles for a 10K increase in temperature, Ea can be found using the formula: ln(k2/k1) = Ea * (T2 - T1) / (R * T1 * T2), where k1 and k2 are rate constants at temperatures T1 and T2 respectively.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Calculating Activation Energy (Ea) in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Fraction of Molecules with Energy ≥ Activation Energy
text:
Fraction of Molecules with Energy ≥ Activation Energy

Key terms: Boltzmann distribution, activation energy, temperature

The fraction of molecules with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy can be calculated using the Boltzmann distribution: N = e-Ea/RT / (1 + e-Ea/RT), where N is the fraction, Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Fraction of Molecules with Energy ≥ Activation Energy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Fraction of Molecules with Energy ≥ Activation Energy in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Chemical Kinetics: Study and Variables
text:
Chemical Kinetics: Study and Variables

Key terms: chemical kinetics, reaction rate, variables

Chemical kinetics is the study of chemical reactions with respect to reaction rates, effect of various variables, rearrangement of atoms, and formation of intermediates. Variables affecting reaction rates include temperature, concentration of reactants, and catalysts.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Chemical Kinetics: Study and Variables in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Rate Law and Order of a Reaction
text:
Rate Law and Order of a Reaction

Key terms: rate law, order of a reaction, concentration

The rate law is a mathematical representation of the rate of a reaction. The order of a reaction with respect to a reactant is the power of its concentration that appears in the rate law equation. The order of a reaction is the sum of all such powers of concentration terms for different reactants.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Rate Law and Order of a Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rate Law and Order of a Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Molecularity vs Order of a Reaction
text:
Molecularity vs Order of a Reaction

Key terms: molecularity, order of a reaction, elementary reaction

Molecularity is defined only for an elementary reaction and has values limited from 1 to 3. Order of a reaction can be 0, 1, 2, 3, or even a fraction. Molecularity and order of an elementary reaction are the same.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Molecularity vs Order of a Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Molecularity vs Order of a Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Arrhenius Equation and Collision Theory
text:
Arrhenius Equation and Collision Theory

Key terms: Arrhenius equation, collision theory, steric factor

The Arrhenius equation describes the temperature dependence of rate constants. Collision theory introduces a steric factor (P) to account for the orientation of molecules which collide, modifying the Arrhenius equation to k = Ae-Ea/RT * P.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Arrhenius Equation and Collision Theory in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Determining Rate Constants and Order of Reaction
text:
Determining Rate Constants and Order of Reaction

Key terms: rate constant, order of a reaction, rate law

Rate constants and the order of a reaction can be determined from the rate law or its integrated rate equation. For example, from the rate expression 3NO(g) → N2O(g), Rate = k[NO]2, the order of the reaction with respect to NO is 2.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Determining Rate Constants and Order of Reaction
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Determining Rate Constants and Order of Reaction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Transition Metals in the Periodic Table
text:
Transition Metals in the Periodic Table

Key terms: d-block, f-block, transition metals

The d-block contains elements of groups 3-12 where d orbitals are progressively filled. The f-block is separate, with 4f and 5f orbitals filled. Transition metals have incomplete d subshells and are studied separately due to their unique properties.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Transition Metals in the Periodic Table
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Transition Metals in the Periodic Table in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electronic Configurations of Transition Elements
text:
Electronic Configurations of Transition Elements

Key terms: electronic configuration, d orbitals, ns orbitals

The general electronic configuration of transition elements is (n-1)d^1-10 ns^1-2, with exceptions due to energy differences between (n-1)d and ns orbitals. Some elements may have half or completely filled d orbitals, which are more stable.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Electronic Configurations of Transition Elements in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidation States of Transition Elements
text:
Oxidation States of Transition Elements

Key terms: oxidation states, d orbitals, stable electron configuration

Transition elements exhibit a variety of oxidation states due to their partly filled d orbitals. This is because these elements can lose electrons from their d orbitals to achieve a stable electron configuration.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Oxidation States of Transition Elements in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Properties of Transition Elements
text:
Properties of Transition Elements

Key terms: metallic properties, catalytic properties, paramagnetic behaviour

Transition elements display typical metallic properties like high tensile strength, ductility, malleability, high thermal and electrical conductivity, and metallic lustre. They also exhibit catalytic properties and paramagnetic behaviour.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Properties of Transition Elements in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Trends in Properties of Transition Elements
text:
Trends in Properties of Transition Elements

Key terms: melting points, enthalpies of atomisation, interatomic interaction

In any row, the melting points of transition metals rise to a maximum at d^5 and fall regularly as the atomic number increases. The enthalpies of atomisation also show maxima at about the middle of each series, indicating that one unpaired electron per d orbital is particularly favourable for strong interatomic interaction.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Trends in Properties of Transition Elements
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Trends in Properties of Transition Elements in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Higher Enthalpies of Atomisation
text:
Higher Enthalpies of Atomisation

Key terms: atomisation, enthalpy, interatomic interaction

Transition elements have higher enthalpies of atomisation due to strong interatomic interaction caused by unpaired electrons.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Higher Enthalpies of Atomisation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionisation Enthalpy Variation
text:
Ionisation Enthalpy Variation

Key terms: ionisation enthalpy, transition elements, non-transition elements

Ionisation enthalpies increase along a series of transition elements, but less than in non-transition elements. The first ionisation enthalpy increases slightly, while the second and third increase more significantly.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ionisation Enthalpy Variation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionisation Enthalpy Irregularity
text:
Ionisation Enthalpy Irregularity

Key terms: ionisation enthalpy, 3d series, electron removal

The first ionisation enthalpy of 3d series metals shows an irregular trend due to the removal of one electron altering the energies of 4s and 3d orbitals.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Ionisation Enthalpy Irregularity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidation States Variability
text:
Oxidation States Variability

Key terms: oxidation states, transition elements, d orbitals

Transition elements exhibit a wide range of oxidation states due to incomplete filling of d orbitals, with elements near the middle of the series showing the most variability.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Oxidation States Variability in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Standard Electrode Potentials
text:
Standard Electrode Potentials

Key terms: standard electrode potential, reduction, enthalpy of atomisation

The standard electrode potentials (E°) for the reduction of M2+ to M vary across the series, with Cu having a positive E° due to its high enthalpy of atomisation and low hydration enthalpy.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Standard Electrode Potentials in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidising Power of Transition Metals
text:
Oxidising Power of Transition Metals

Key terms: oxidising power, transition metals, reduction

The oxidising power of transition metals in the VO2+ < Cr2O72- < MnO4- series increases due to the increasing stability of the lower species they are reduced to.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxidising Power of Transition Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Irregular Eo Values for First Row Transition Metals
text:
Irregular Eo Values for First Row Transition Metals

Key terms: Eo values, ionisation enthalpies, sublimation enthalpies

The Eo values for the first row transition metals are irregular due to the variation in ionisation enthalpies and sublimation enthalpies, particularly for Mn3+/Mn2+ which has a much larger third ionisation energy.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Irregular Eo Values for First Row Transition Metals
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Irregular Eo Values for First Row Transition Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Chemical Reactivity of Transition Metals
text:
Chemical Reactivity of Transition Metals

Key terms: chemical reactivity, transition metals, Eo values

Transition metals vary in chemical reactivity, with most being sufficiently electropositive to dissolve in mineral acids, but some being 'noble' and unaffected. The Eo values indicate a decreasing tendency to form divalent cations across the series.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Chemical Reactivity of Transition Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Magnetic Properties of Transition Metals
text:
Magnetic Properties of Transition Metals

Key terms: magnetic properties, transition metals, paramagnetism, unpaired electrons

Transition metals exhibit magnetic properties, with many being paramagnetic due to the presence of unpaired electrons. The magnetic moment increases with the number of unpaired electrons.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Properties of Transition Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Formation of Coloured Ions by Transition Metals
text:
Formation of Coloured Ions by Transition Metals

Key terms: coloured ions, transition metals, electron excitation, light absorption

Transition metals form coloured ions in aqueous solutions due to electron excitation from lower energy d orbitals to higher energy d orbitals, with the colour observed being the complementary colour of the light absorbed.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Formation of Coloured Ions by Transition Metals
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Formation of Coloured Ions by Transition Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Disproportionation of Oxidation States
text:
Disproportionation of Oxidation States

Key terms: disproportionation, oxidation states, manganese

Disproportionation occurs when a particular oxidation state becomes less stable relative to other oxidation states, with an example being manganese(VI) disproportionating to manganese(VII) and manganese(IV) in acidic solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Disproportionation of Oxidation States in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxides and Oxoanions of Metals
text:
Oxides and Oxoanions of Metals

Key terms: oxides, oxoanions, metals, oxidation numbers

Metals form oxides and oxoanions with varying oxidation numbers, ionic character, and acidic/basic properties. The highest oxidation number in oxides coincides with the group number, and some metals also form oxocations.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxides and Oxoanions of Metals in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Preparation and Properties of Potassium Dichromate
text:
Preparation and Properties of Potassium Dichromate

Key terms: potassium dichromate, preparation, oxidising agent, leather industry, volumetric analysis

Potassium dichromate is prepared from chromite ore and is a strong oxidising agent. It is used in leather industry and as a primary standard in volumetric analysis.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Preparation and Properties of Potassium Dichromate
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Preparation and Properties of Potassium Dichromate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Preparation of Potassium Permanganate
text:
Preparation of Potassium Permanganate

Key terms: Potassium Permanganate, MnO2, Electrolytic Oxidation, Peroxodisulphate

Potassium permanganate is prepared by the alkaline oxidative fusion of MnO2 followed by electrolytic oxidation of manganate (V). It is also prepared in the lab by oxidizing a manganese (II) ion salt with peroxodisulphate.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Preparation of Potassium Permanganate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidizing Properties of Potassium Permanganate
text:
Oxidizing Properties of Potassium Permanganate

Key terms: Oxidizing Agent, Iodide, Fe2+, Oxalate, Hydrogen Sulphide, Nitrite, Thiosulphate, Manganous Salt

Potassium permanganate is a strong oxidizing agent. In acid solutions, it oxidizes iodide to iodine, Fe2+ to Fe3+, oxalate to carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulphide to sulphur, and nitrite to nitrate. In neutral or faintly alkaline solutions, it oxidizes iodide to iodate, thiosulphate to sulphate, and manganous salt to MnO2.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Oxidizing Properties of Potassium Permanganate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Half-Reactions of Potassium Permanganate
text:
Half-Reactions of Potassium Permanganate

Key terms: Half-Reactions, Reduction Potential, Hydrogen Ions, Permanganate, Manganate, Manganese Dioxide, Manganese(II) Salt

The half-reactions of potassium permanganate in its reduction to manganate, manganese dioxide, and manganese(II) salt involve the transfer of one, four, and eight electrons, respectively. The reduction potential of permanganate is influenced by the concentration of hydrogen ions in the solution.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Half-Reactions of Potassium Permanganate in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Lanthanoid Series
text:
Lanthanoid Series

Key terms: Lanthanoids, Lanthanoid Contraction, Oxidation States, Cerium, Praseodymium, Terbium, Dysprosium, Europium, Ytterbium

The lanthanoids are a series of 15 elements following lanthanum. They have similar chemical properties and a unique decrease in atomic and ionic radii, known as lanthanoid contraction. They have only one stable oxidation state, +3, except for Ce, Pr, Tb, and Dy which can also exhibit +4, and Eu and Yb which can exhibit +2.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Lanthanoid Series in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Actinoid Series
text:
Actinoid Series

Key terms: Actinoids, Radioactivity, Half-Life, Actinium, Lawrencium

The actinoids are a series of 14 elements following actinium. They have variable occupancy of the 5f and 6d subshells and are radioactive. The earlier members have relatively long half-lives, while the latter ones have half-life values ranging from a day to 3 minutes for lawrencium.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Actinoid Series in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Lanthanoid vs Actinoid Contraction
text:
Lanthanoid vs Actinoid Contraction

Key terms: lanthanoid contraction, actinoid contraction, 5f electrons

Both lanthanoids and actinoids exhibit a decrease in size across their series, known as contraction. Actinoid contraction is greater due to poor shielding by 5f electrons.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Lanthanoid vs Actinoid Contraction in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidation States of Actinoids
text:
Oxidation States of Actinoids

Key terms: oxidation states, actinoids, +3 state, +4 state

Actinoids show a variety of oxidation states, with +3 being the most common. The first half of the series often exhibits higher oxidation states, while the latter half shows a decrease.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Oxidation States of Actinoids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Electronic Configurations of Actinoids
text:
Electronic Configurations of Actinoids

Key terms: electronic configurations, f orbitals, 5f, 4f

Actinoids have electronic configurations related to the stabilities of f orbital occupancies (f^0, f^7, f^14). The 5f orbitals participate more in bonding than 4f orbitals due to less burial.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Electronic Configurations of Actinoids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Actinoid Metals' Reactivity
text:
Actinoid Metals' Reactivity

Key terms: reactivity, actinoid metals, water, non-metals, hydrochloric acid

Actinoid metals are highly reactive, especially when finely divided. They react with water, non-metals, and are attacked by hydrochloric acid. Alkalies have no action on them.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Actinoid Metals' Reactivity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Magnetic Properties of Actinoids
text:
Magnetic Properties of Actinoids

Key terms: magnetic properties, actinoids, lanthanoids, magnetic susceptibility

The magnetic properties of actinoids are more complex than those of lanthanoids. Although they have roughly parallel magnetic susceptibility, lanthanoids have higher values.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Magnetic Properties of Actinoids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionization Enthalpies of Actinoids
text:
Ionization Enthalpies of Actinoids

Key terms: ionization enthalpies, actinoids, lanthanoids, 5f electrons

Early actinoids have lower ionization enthalpies than early lanthanoids. This is due to more effective shielding of 5f electrons from the nuclear charge, making outer electrons more available for bonding.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Ionization Enthalpies of Actinoids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Comparison with Lanthanoids
text:
Comparison with Lanthanoids

Key terms: comparison, actinoids, lanthanoids, oxidation states

Actinoids resemble lanthanoids in having more compounds in the +3 state than in the +4 state. However, +3 and +4 ions tend to hydrolyse, making it unsatisfactory to review their chemistry in terms of oxidation states.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Comparison with Lanthanoids in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Actinoid Oxidation States
text:
Actinoid Oxidation States

Key terms: actinoids, lanthanoids, oxidation states

The chemistry of actinoids is less smooth than lanthanoids due to variations in oxidation states. For example, uranium can have oxidation states ranging from +3 to +6.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Actinoid Oxidation States in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Last Actinoid Element
text:
Last Actinoid Element

Key terms: lawrencium, electronic configuration, oxidation state

The last element in the actinoid series is lawrencium (Z=103) with electronic configuration [Rn]7s^27p^17f^14. Its possible oxidation state is +3.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Last Actinoid Element in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Silver as a Transition Element
text:
Silver as a Transition Element

Key terms: silver, transition element, d-orbitals

Silver (Z=47) can exhibit a +2 oxidation state, making it a transition element, as it has incompletely filled d-orbitals (4d).

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Silver as a Transition Element in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Zinc's Metallic Bonding
text:
Zinc's Metallic Bonding

Key terms: zinc, metallic bonds, 3d-orbitals

In zinc, no electrons from 3d-orbitals are involved in the formation of metallic bonds, unlike other metals in the 3d series.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Zinc's Metallic Bonding in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Manganese's Unpaired Electrons
text:
Manganese's Unpaired Electrons

Key terms: manganese, unpaired electrons, 3d series

Manganese (Z=25) has the maximum number of unpaired electrons among its atoms, making it unique in the 3d series.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Manganese's Unpaired Electrons in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionization Enthalpy Variation
text:
Ionization Enthalpy Variation

Key terms: ionization enthalpies, 3d series, d configurations

The irregular variation of ionization enthalpies in the 3d series is mainly due to the varying stability of different 3d configurations, such as d^0, d^5, and d^10.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Ionization Enthalpy Variation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidation by Oxygen or Fluorine
text:
Oxidation by Oxygen or Fluorine

Key terms: oxidation, oxygen, fluorine, metals

Due to their small size and high electronegativity, oxygen or fluorine can oxidize metals to their highest oxidation states.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Oxidation by Oxygen or Fluorine in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Copper Disproportionation
text:
Copper Disproportionation

Key terms: copper, disproportionation, E^0

In aqueous solution, Cu^+ undergoes disproportionation, i.e., 2Cu^+(aq) → Cu^2+(aq) + Cu(s), with a favorable E^0 value.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Copper Disproportionation in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Compounds
text:
Coordination Compounds

Key terms: Coordination Compounds, Transition Metals, Complex Compounds

Complex compounds formed when metal atoms bind to anions or neutral molecules by sharing electrons. Important in modern inorganic chemistry, bio-inorganic chemistry, and industry.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Coordination Compounds in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Werner's Theory of Coordination Compounds
text:
Werner's Theory of Coordination Compounds

Key terms: Werner's Theory, Primary Valence, Secondary Valence, Coordination Polyhedra

Alfred Werner's theory proposing that metals in coordination compounds exhibit primary and secondary valences, with secondary valences forming coordination polyhedra.

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Werner's Theory of Coordination Compounds in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Entity
text:
Coordination Entity

Key terms: Coordination Entity, Central Atom/Ion, Ligands

A central metal atom or ion bonded to a fixed number of ions or molecules, forming a coordination entity like [CoCl3(NH3)3].

metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Coordination Entity in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Number
text:
Coordination Number

Key terms: Coordination Number, Ligand Donor Atoms

The number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to a metal ion in a complex, e.g., [PtCl6]2- has a coordination number of 6.

Coordination Sphere

The central atom/ion and the ligands attached to it, enclosed in square brackets, e.g., [Fe(CN)6]4- is the coordination sphere in K4[Fe(CN)6].

Coordination Polyhedron

Key terms: Coordination Polyhedron, Octahedral, Square Planar, Tetrahedral

The spatial arrangement of ligand atoms directly attached to the central atom, forming common polyhedra like octahedral, square planar, and tetrahedral.

Nomenclature of Coordination Compounds

Systematic naming of coordination compounds based on IUPAC recommendations, listing ligands in alphabetical order and indicating charges.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Oxidation Number of Central Atom
text:
Oxidation Number of Central Atom

Key terms: Oxidation Number, Central Atom, Ligands

The charge a central atom would carry if all ligands and shared electron pairs were removed, e.g., Cu(I) in [Cu(CN)4]3-.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Naming Coordination Compounds
text:
Naming Coordination Compounds

Key terms: cation, ligand, prefix, oxidation state

Coordination compounds are named using specific rules. The cation is named first, followed by ligands in alphabetical order. Prefixes indicate the number of ligands, and the oxidation state of the metal is indicated by Roman numerals.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Isomerism in Coordination Compounds
text:
Isomerism in Coordination Compounds

Key terms: isomer, geometric, optical, linkage, coordination, ionisation, solvate

Isomers are compounds with the same formula but different structures. Coordination compounds can exhibit geometric, optical, linkage, coordination, ionisation, and solvate isomerism.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Bonding in Coordination Compounds
text:
Bonding in Coordination Compounds

Key terms: Valence Bond Theory, hybrid orbitals, magnetic behavior

Valence Bond Theory explains bonding in coordination compounds. The metal ion uses its orbitals to form hybrid orbitals that overlap with ligand orbitals. The geometry of a complex can be predicted from its magnetic behavior.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Bonding in Coordination Compounds in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Ionisation Isomers
text:
Ionisation Isomers

Key terms: ionisation isomer, counter ion, ligand

Ionisation isomers are coordination compounds where the counter ion can displace a ligand, becoming the counter ion itself. This results in different compounds with the same formula.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Optical Isomers
text:
Optical Isomers

Key terms: optical isomer, mirror image, chiral, didentate ligand

Optical isomers are mirror images that cannot be superimposed. In coordination compounds, optical isomerism is common in octahedral complexes involving didentate ligands.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Tetrahedral Hybridisation in Ni(II) Complexes
text:
Tetrahedral Hybridisation in Ni(II) Complexes

Key terms: tetrahedral, hybridisation, paramagnetic, unpaired electrons

Nickel(II) forms tetrahedral complexes like [NiCl4]2- and [Ni(CO)4] with four ligands using sp3 hybrid orbitals. Each ligand donates a pair of electrons. The complex is paramagnetic if it contains unpaired electrons, like [NiCl4]2- with two unpaired electrons.

Square Planar Hybridisation in Ni(II) Complexes

Key terms: square planar, hybridisation, diamagnetic, unpaired electrons

Nickel(II) also forms square planar complexes like [Ni(CN)4]2- using dsp2 hybrid orbitals. Each cyanide ion donates a pair of electrons, making the complex diamagnetic with no unpaired electrons.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Crystal Field Splitting in Octahedral Complexes
text:
Crystal Field Splitting in Octahedral Complexes

Key terms: crystal field splitting, t2g, eg, Do, spectrochemical series

In an octahedral complex, the d orbitals split into two sets: t2g (lower energy) and eg (higher energy) due to crystal field splitting. The energy separation is denoted by Do. Ligands can be arranged in a spectrochemical series based on their field strength.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | High Spin and Low Spin Complexes
text:
High Spin and Low Spin Complexes

Key terms: high spin, low spin, Do, P, strong field ligands, weak field ligands

For d4 to d7 ions, the fourth electron may enter the eg level (high spin complex) if Do < P (pairing energy), or the t2g level (low spin complex) if Do > P. Strong field ligands form low spin complexes, while weak field ligands form high spin complexes.

text:
Colour in Coordination Compounds

Key terms: colour, d-d transitions, crystal field theory, complementary colour

Coordination compounds absorb light in the visible region, causing them to appear coloured. The colour is due to d-d transitions of electrons, as explained by crystal field theory. The complementary colour is observed.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Crystal Field Splitting in Tetrahedral Complexes
text:
Crystal Field Splitting in Tetrahedral Complexes

Key terms: tetrahedral, d orbital splitting, low spin configurations

In tetrahedral complexes, the d orbital splitting is inverted and smaller compared to octahedral complexes. The energy splitting is not sufficient to force pairing, so low spin configurations are rarely observed.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Limitations of Crystal Field Theory
text:
Limitations of Crystal Field Theory

Key terms: limitations, crystal field theory, ligand field theory, molecular orbital theory

Crystal field theory has limitations, such as assuming ligands are point charges and not accounting for covalent character in bonding. Ligand field theory and molecular orbital theory provide more accurate explanations.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Limitations of Crystal Field Theory in Grade 12 Chemistry.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Metal Carbonyl Bonding
text:
Metal Carbonyl Bonding

Key terms: Metal-Carbon Bond, Synergic Effect, Crystal Field Theory

In metal carbonyls, the metal-carbon bond has both s and p character. The M–C s bond forms from the donation of lone pair electrons on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant orbital of the metal. The M–C p bond forms from the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled d orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding p* orbital of carbon monoxide. This synergic effect strengthens the bond between CO and the metal.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Compounds in Biology
text:
Coordination Compounds in Biology

Key terms: Chlorophyll, Haemoglobin, Vitamin B12

Coordination compounds play crucial roles in biological systems. Examples include chlorophyll, a coordination compound of magnesium, which is responsible for photosynthesis. Haemoglobin, a coordination compound of iron, acts as an oxygen carrier in blood. Vitamin B12, a coordination compound of cobalt, is essential for human health.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Compounds in Industry
text:
Coordination Compounds in Industry

Key terms: Catalysts, Electroplating, Industrial Processes

Coordination compounds have wide industrial applications. They are used as catalysts for many processes, such as the hydrogenation of alkenes using a rhodium complex. They also facilitate smooth and even electroplating of articles with silver and gold from solutions of the complexes [Ag(CN)2]– and [Au(CN)2]–.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Chemistry | Coordination Compounds in Medicine
text:
Coordination Compounds in Medicine

Key terms: EDTA, Cis-platin, Chelate Therapy

Coordination compounds have significant roles in medicine. EDTA, a chelating ligand, is used in the treatment of lead poisoning. Some coordination compounds of platinum, like cis-platin, effectively inhibit the growth of tumours. Growing interest lies in the use of chelate therapy in medicinal chemistry.

text:
Crystal Field Theory (CFT)

Key terms: Crystal Field Theory, Crystal Field, d Orbital Splitting

CFT explains the formation, magnetic behavior, and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds. It is based on the effect of different crystal fields provided by ligands, which are treated as point charges. The splitting of d orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

Coordination compounds are of great importance in various fields. They are widely present in mineral, plant, and animal worlds, and play many important functions in analytical chemistry, metallurgy, biological systems, industry, and medicine. They are also used in qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis, estimation of hardness of water, and extraction processes of metals.

The magnetic moment of a complex ion is determined by the number of unpaired electrons. Ions with more unpaired electrons have higher magnetic moments.

The stability of a complex ion depends on the nature of the ligands and the metal ion. Complexes with stronger ligands and more charges are generally more stable.
